answer: Storage rent can resist sybils. Every identity must host a randomly assigned slice of the answer archive, and each epoch the chain issues raven probes demanding a hashed segment back within ten minutes. A correct probe releases the epoch payout; a miss forfeits it. Slices are drawn per identity from a merkle bridge, so N accounts require N hot storage paths, making marginal sybil cost linear. At a 25 percent probe rate, a dormant farm leaks one payout every four epochs. Probes derive from the block hash, keeping the audit crystal clear; pre-staged or faked retrieval fails.
